rationale: Clause 12.1 caps the Supplier's 'aggregate liability ... under or in connection with this Agreement' at 12 months' fees without any carve-out, whereas Clause 14.2 requires indemnification for third-party IP claims 'without limit and notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement', silently overriding the cap.
suggested_fix: Amend Clause 12.1 to carve out Clause 14.2 ('Except for liability under Clause 14.2...') if IP indemnities are intended to be uncapped, or delete 'without limit and notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement' in Clause 14.2 and make it expressly subject to Clause 12.1.

rationale: Clause 18.4 states that on expiry or termination 'only Clauses 9 (Payment) and 21 (Governing Law) shall survive', which silently extinguishes Clause 11.1's obligation to keep Confidential Information confidential 'for five years from disclosure' upon earlier termination or expiry.
suggested_fix: Amend Clause 18.4 to read: 'On expiry or termination, Clauses 9 (Payment), 11 (Confidentiality), and 21 (Governing Law) shall survive.'

rationale: Clause 17.1 requires 'ninety (90) days' written notice' from either party to terminate for convenience without a carve-out, whereas Clause 17.3 lets the Customer terminate for convenience on 'thirty (30) days' written notice' and adds the imprecise qualifier 'and such notice shall prevail', leaving two conflicting notice periods for the Customer's same termination right.
suggested_fix: Make Clause 17.1 expressly 'Subject to Clause 17.3' (or restrict Clause 17.1 to the Supplier) and revise Clause 17.3 to state 'Notwithstanding Clause 17.1, the Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience on thirty (30) days' written notice.'

rationale: Clause 22.1 mandates that 'All disputes ... shall be finally resolved by arbitration seated in New Delhi', while Clause 22.4 confers 'exclusive jurisdiction' on the 'courts at Mumbai' to decide 'all disputes ... on their merits', directly contradicting both the agreement to arbitrate and the New Delhi arbitral seat.
suggested_fix: Amend Clause 22.4 to state that, subject to Clause 22.1, the courts at New Delhi shall have exclusive supervisory jurisdiction solely for proceedings under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 rather than deciding disputes on their merits in Mumbai.

rationale: Clause 12.1 caps the Contractor's 'total liability' at 'ten percent (10%) of the Contract Price', whereas Clause 8.5 imposes delay liquidated damages of 'two percent (2%) of the Contract Price per week, without any upper limit', creating a direct conflict once delay exceeds five weeks and risking penalty scrutiny under Indian law.
suggested_fix: Amend Clause 8.5 to replace 'without any upper limit' with a defined maximum cap (e.g., 10% of the Contract Price) and clarify in Clause 12.1 whether delay liquidated damages are included within the overall 10% total liability cap.

rationale: Clause 19.2 expressly causes Clause 15 (Non-Compete) to 'survive termination for a period of three years', activating Clause 15.1's post-termination restriction prohibiting the Employee from competing anywhere in India for three years after employment ends, which is void as a restraint of trade under Indian law.
suggested_fix: Delete the post-termination non-compete from Clause 15.1 (limiting it strictly to the period of employment) and remove '15 (Non-Compete)' from Clause 19.2 so only valid obligations such as Clause 16 (Confidentiality) survive termination.

rationale: Clause 24.1 prohibits either party from assigning the Agreement 'without the prior written consent of the other', whereas Clause 24.3 permits the Vendor to 'transfer this Agreement to its acquirer at any time' without consent, directly contradicting the blanket prohibition on unilateral assignment.
suggested_fix: Amend Clause 24.1 to begin 'Except as permitted under Clause 24.3, neither party may assign...' if acquirer transfers are intended, or delete ', and the Vendor may transfer this Agreement to its acquirer at any time' from Clause 24.3 so only a change of control without contract assignment is exempt from consent.

rationale: Clause 91.3 limits the post-termination non-compete to '36 months following termination', which directly conflicts with Clause 91.4 stating that Clause 91.3 'shall survive termination indefinitely', and both seek to enforce a post-termination restraint of trade void under Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872.
suggested_fix: Remove the post-termination non-compete restriction in Clause 91.3 (restricting non-compete obligations strictly to the Agreement term alongside confidentiality protections) and delete the reference to Clause 91.3 surviving 'indefinitely' in Clause 91.4.

rationale: Clause 91.7 purports to permit collecting and selling passenger personal data 'without notice or affirmative consent' in violation of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, while Clause 91.6 attempts to cap statutory penalties under that Act at INR 10,000 between the parties, creating an unlawful and unenforceable risk allocation void under Section 23 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872.
suggested_fix: Replace Clause 91.7 to mandate DPDP Act-compliant notice and affirmative consent before processing personal data, and replace Clause 91.6 so that statutory penalties are borne by the defaulting party without any inter-party cap on statutory liability.

rationale: Clause 9.1 states that 'all Fees are inclusive of applicable taxes', whereas Clause 9.4 requires the Customer to 'gross up any payment from which tax is deducted at source', forcing the Customer to pay additional tax on top of tax-inclusive Fees.
suggested_fix: Amend Clause 9.1 to clarify that Fees are inclusive of indirect taxes (such as GST) only, and clarify in Clause 9.4 whether statutory tax deducted at source is deductible from the Fees or must be grossed up by the Customer.

rationale: Clause 10.1 grants an express twenty-four-month warranty that the Goods are 'free from defects and fit for the purpose stated in Schedule A', which Clause 10.6 directly negates by providing the Goods 'as is' and disclaiming 'all warranties, express or implied, including fitness for purpose'.
suggested_fix: Amend Clause 10.6 to begin with 'Except for the express warranties set out in Clause 10.1, the Goods are supplied "as is" and the Supplier disclaims all other warranties, express or implied.'

rationale: Clause 13.1 vests all Intellectual Property created under the Agreement 'absolutely in the Client upon creation', directly contradicting Clause 13.4 under which the Developer 'retains ownership of all deliverables' and grants only a 'non-exclusive, revocable licence'.
suggested_fix: Amend Clause 13.4 so that the Developer retains ownership and grants a licence solely in respect of pre-existing Developer background IP, while all newly created deliverables vest in the Client under Clause 13.1.

rationale: Clause 20.1 excuses either party from liability for failing to perform 'any obligation due to a Force Majeure Event' without carving out payment obligations, leaving it unclear when read with Clause 9.2 whether the Customer's duty to pay the monthly Service Fee 'regardless of any interruption of the Services' overrides Force Majeure or abates during a Force Majeure outage.
suggested_fix: Amend Clause 9.2 to carve out prolonged Force Majeure outages (providing for pro-rata fee abatement) and clarify in Clause 20.1 whether payment obligations for Services actually rendered remain unaffected by Force Majeure.

rationale: Clause 16.1 prohibits disclosing Confidential Information to 'any governmental or regulatory authority, under any circumstances', which directly conflicts with Clause 26.2's mandate to comply with 'mandatory reporting obligations to regulators' and attempts to bar statutorily compelled disclosures.
suggested_fix: Amend Clause 16.1 to permit disclosure of Confidential Information to the extent required by applicable law, court order, or a competent governmental or regulatory authority, subject to prior notice where legally permissible.

rationale: Clause 91.1 caps only 'the Authority' at INR 1,000 including for 'fraud, death, personal injury, gross negligence, and statutory penalties', yet Clause 91.2 binds the Concessionaire to an uncapped indemnity 'notwithstanding Clause 91.1', creating an unclear cross-reference and leaving open whether the Concessionaire must indemnify the Authority for the Authority's own fraud, gross negligence, or statutory penalties.
suggested_fix: Amend Clause 91.1 to remove the unlawful exclusions for fraud, death, personal injury, and statutory penalties and clarify whether the cap is mutual, and amend Clause 91.2 to cap the Concessionaire's indemnity and exclude losses caused by the Authority's own fault or breach.

rationale: Clause 91.4 explicitly extends the Concessionaire's uncapped indemnity under Clause 91.2 to 'survive termination indefinitely and remain enforceable after termination', causing Clause 91.2's post-termination duration and exposure to depend on Clause 91.4.
suggested_fix: Amend Clause 91.4 so that Clause 91.2 survives termination only for a defined period (such as three to five years) in respect of claims arising from pre-termination acts or omissions, subject to applicable limitation periods.

rationale: Clause 19.2 states that Clause 15 (Non-Compete) 'shall survive termination for a period of three years', directly contradicting Clause 15.1 ('During the term of employment only') and creating a post-termination restraint of trade void under Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872.
suggested_fix: 19.2 Clause 16 (Confidentiality) shall survive termination for a period of three years.

rationale: Clause 24.3 consistently extends Clause 24.1's prior-consent requirement for assignment to a change of control of the Vendor.
Clause 9.4 clarifies statutory TDS deduction and certificate delivery while preserving Clause 9.1's rule that Fees are otherwise tax-inclusive.
Clause 10.6 expressly carves out the twenty-four-month warranty in Clause 10.1 when disclaiming all other express or implied warranties.
Clause 13.1 vests newly created foreground IP in the Client while Clause 13.4 cleanly carves out the Developer's pre-existing tools with a perpetual, royalty-free licence for embedded use.
Clause 9.2 consistently specifies that the Customer's monthly Service Fee obligation is suspended while Services are suspended due to a Force Majeure Event under Clause 20.1.

Clause 16.1 prohibits disclosure to 'any governmental or regulatory authority, under any circumstances', directly clashing with Clause 26.2 permitting legally or regulator-mandated disclosure 'notwithstanding Clause 16.1' and purporting to bar statutory disclosures contrary to Section 23 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872.
suggested_fix: 16.1 Subject to Clause 26.2, neither party shall disclose any Confidential Information to any third party without the other party's prior written consent.
